key_insight: Diversity among quantum and classical model architectures can be exploited through combinatorial fusion to outperform the single best model.
engineering_relevance: For quantum machine learning pipelines, this suggests that keeping and combining multiple strong but diverse VQC designs may yield more robust and accurate predictors than selecting only one architecture.
method: Built a pool of 29 diverse classical and quantum models.
Applied Combinatorial Fusion Analysis (CFA) using rank-score function and cognitive diversity to choose and combine models.
Used both score fusion and rank fusion over maximally diverse subsets.
evidence_signal: Across four binary classification benchmarks, CFA-based hybrid classical-quantum fusion outperformed the best individual model on every dataset, with accuracy gains up to 6.03%.
watch_item: The gains depend on having a diverse candidate pool and careful subset selection, so performance may be less reliable if the search space is small or poorly sampled.
paper_title: Diversity-Aware Ensemble of Quantum-Classical Models via Combinatorial Fusion
